rows.name: a turn waiting on a person asks through the client, or says how to answer
an agent's MCP endpoint takes whatever may prompt it, and no other tenant's token
a message streams progress, is sent once when called again, and a full queue is busy
a tenant's own OpenRouter key answers its decisions, and is not charged
the decide builtin answers from codemode in batches and directly, billed to the run and the agent
an agent that denies data collection has decide by default, its calls sent with that data policy
decide is every agent's by default, and opts out with decide: false on the agent, its update or its definition; a toolless run and a tenant without an OpenRouter key have none
POST /v1/decisions answers one state or a batch on the platform's OpenRouter key, bills what OpenRouter charged, and logs no state
a browser token with the children scope reads its agent's sub-agents, and only theirs
a child that waits on a person notifies its parent, and notifies again when it resumes and ends
a parent messages its finished child, which works again with its history and notifies again; a child messages its parent
two agents messaging each other in a loop stop at the wake cap with agent_loop_limit, and a turn sends at most 20 messages
interrupt_agent aborts a child; aborting the parent aborts its children unless children: keep; deleting it deletes the children it made
a child's message joins its busy parent's running turn at its next step, without a turn of its own
a child's message cuts its parent's wait_agent short, and the parent reads it next
a response that starts a sub-agent and, beside it, messages and waits for it: those calls run once it has started
a background child's progress rides on its parent's next tool result, latest only and once, without a turn; an ending supersedes it
a message to a sub-agent that already answered starts a turn, and wait_agent waits for that turn's answer, not the earlier one
a sub-agent of the model's own design gets its instructions with its task, as its first message; one from a definition keeps its own prompt
a sub-agent of the model's own design shares its parent's files at the same paths
wait_agent with untilProgress returns on a report it has not seen, after its floor, so the parent can correct a sub-agent mid-run
a delegate child's progress reaches its parent's watchers as subagent_progress and the delegate call's progress
only a sub-agent reports progress, and a report is short
spawn_agent refuses past maxParallel running children and past the depth limit
two agents waking each other through notifications stop at the wake cap with agent_loop_limit, the notification still in history
a child's spend is charged to its parent when its notification lands, and a parent at its spend limit gets no turn
aborting a parent while a child's notification waits keeps the notification: it lands without a turn
spawn_agent returns at once, and the child's ending arrives once, as a notification with its source and marker
children started together share what the parent may spend, and limits alone bound a tool's spawns without a tool for the model
wait_agent answers a child's ending in its result, so no notification follows; list_agents lists children
code fans out three delegates once, returns their structured answers, and records each child
a script returning without awaiting a delegate stops that child
scripts waiting on children longer than their deadline, on an account with one code slot, finish: the wait is off their clock and holds no slot
workflow input is refused on agents, definitions, runs, upserts and configure; stored settings are ignored
parallel children share what their parent's run has left, rather than each getting all of it
children of one response share what their parent's run has left even when they run one after another
a caller cannot move a run's place in the delegation chain with prompt metadata
delegate starts a child from a definition, returns its answer, and links it to its parent
aborting a parent aborts the children it waits on; the stream shows them to subscribers that ask
aborting a parent answers once its delegate child has ended, charges what the child spent, and deleting the parent deletes the child
a delegate child whose ending no call took, its parent's run over, is landed by the sweep and charged to the parent
delegate calls in one response run at once, at most maxParallel together, and one with output answers in its schema
delegation stops at its depth limit, and a run's spend limit bounds its children and counts what they spent
SDK: delegate settings on upsert bring their builtin; a run lists its child's id, and a stream with subagents shows it start and end
a trusted tool prepares a persistent worker and starts it as a background sub-agent; a busy worker queues the next task
a spawn directive from a tool without runtime auth (an attached application's) is refused
abort cancels waiting inputs and closes the turn without the model; expiry does the same
only whoever started the turn, or an approver, may answer
an approval policy asks before a gated tool runs: the approved call runs once, with proof; a declined one never runs
an MCP server's input_required (form and url, and the older -32042) suspends the call; the retry carries the answers and its state
an agent with no one to ask does not tell servers it can elicit
an attached tool asks with ctx.confirm and ctx.ask: the call runs again with the answers, everything before an ask included
inputs from parallel calls are one suspension: answered together, all or none, and listed in the tenant's inbox
an application answers with onInput, from its SDK
a remote MCP tool sets its own exposure in _meta, over its source's; approval keeps its exposure
an input for particular people must be answered naming who answers
code's calls that ask at once are one suspension: an approved one runs, a declined one rejects in the script
code pauses for people: an approval, a question and an MCP form, a run each, and every finished call runs once
ask_user suspends the turn; the answer, after the agent unloaded, resumes it with the answer as the call's result
a new message supersedes a waiting input; its call is closed and the prompt runs
a judge that cannot answer asks the person rather than letting the call run
an approval mode that is not one of the four is refused when the definition is saved
after an approval, a judged call in the resumed turn is still judged against the request that started it
a description longer than the model sees is cut for the judge, not refused
a judged call the judge calls ordinary runs with nobody asked, and the judge sees the request and the arguments
a judged call the judge calls exfiltration does not run, and the model reads the denial as the call's result
a judged call the judge is unsure about asks the person, and the approved call runs without a second judgement
a tool's result is cut at MAX_RESULT characters, saying so
AGENT_ISSUER must be one of the origins served
an alias serves everything, names MCP resources as reached, keeps the issuer, and sends browser pages to the public URL
MCP clients sign in with OAuth: registration, consent, PKCE, rotating refresh tokens, revocation
the hosted MCP endpoint runs the CLI's tools as the caller, and reads no files or environment
the OpenAI apps domain challenge is served as plain text from AGENT_OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE
the operations endpoint names its own protected resource, and answers nobody who is not signed in
only the tenants on AGENT_OPS_ADMINS connect: anyone else is refused at consent, and /mcp is untouched
the tools: read-only rows a dashboard charts, and a token that works here works nowhere else
web_fetch has Firecrawl render JavaScript shells, and only those, charging a platform render
a definition pins web_search's providers; a platform search is charged at the answering provider's price and counted in the hour's ledger entry
a search key the operator set for a tenant (its apiKeys) is used, and is not counted as the platform's
an operator's tenant without a key of its own searches on the platform's, recorded as platform usage and never charged; its own key wins; platformKeys: false keeps the refusal
codemode's searches on the platform's key stop once the tenant's credit is spent, without waiting for the next model request
web_search uses the tenant's own search key, else the platform's billed to credit, and pairs with web_fetch
X search works in agents and stateless runs, uses tenant keys first and bills only platform requests
the application's own connection still answers a replay gap with 409 unless it asks for a snapshot, as relays that do not read snapshots expect
a run for an agent whose tools need its application is refused while none is connected, after a short wait for one reconnecting
the application's ready event carries the hash of the tools it last declared, so an SDK reconfigures only on a change; a run's outcome carries its usage
one application serves an agent's tools at a time: another connection is refused unless it takes over, and the replaced one is told why
a connection that holds an agent but no longer answers (half-open) is replaced without a takeover
an agent takes builtins without a definition: at creation, by upsert and by configuration, and only from its tenant
web_fetch reads public pages as text, from the model and codemode, and never reaches inside
web_fetch refuses internal addresses when nothing is allowed
an agent schedules, lists and cancels its own wake-ups, and wakes up
a schedule of an agent at its spend limit records the 402 and moves to its next occurrence instead of retrying
codemode runs on V8 for every tenant, and the limits API refuses an engine
an upsert's mcpServers are part of its configuration and configHash
a stateless run calls its own MCP servers
an agent without a definition has MCP servers of its own, called with identity tokens that name it and no definition
an agent's or run's own MCP servers take no credentials, and an agent from a definition takes none of its own
tool lists refresh when the server says they changed, and edits keep sealed credentials
applying a definition lists its servers afresh: a tool added without a list_changed notice reaches the agent at once
an agent shows every tool source and what its model gets, connecting to MCP servers only when asked
MCP servers must be on public addresses, checked when saved and again when connecting
a server that only speaks the older SSE transport is reached through it
tool servers get the model's call id, codemode's too, and the actor; their progress reaches the event stream
a burst of progress is coalesced per call: the stream gets the first, then the latest of each window, and the last before the result
a call that keeps reporting progress outlasts its timeout, which limits only silence
an MCP server's tools reach the model and codemode; its credentials are sealed and go only to it
a tool source that cannot be listed is named in every run's outcome
an MCP server is listed when its definition is saved: refused credentials are a 400 then, and what it lists or why it could not is in the answer
a direct tool's large result is cut for the model, as codemode's output is, with the whole of it saved to the workspace
history and forks keep capped tool details and deduplicated prompts without changing model content
every tool call carries a stable idempotency key: MCP servers in _meta, OpenAPI operations as an Idempotency-Key header
calls whose ids repeat across turns (as providers that number calls per response give them) get keys of their own
a run's outcome lists its tool calls, those from code too, by name and id with how each went, the first 100 only
an attached tool's own timeoutMs bounds its call; progress extends it; a timeout is an unknown outcome, in the run's outcome too
the console registers the tools with the browser, runs them as the signed-in tenant, and unregisters on sign-out
in the console, the tools authenticate with the session cookie and the console header, not a key
